papers.title: Thermochemical Rossby waves in rapid rotation: from swallowtail geometry to nonlinear selection
papers.abstract: When heat and solute both destabilise a rapidly rotating fluid, do their buoyancies add? Codensity models assume so, giving a straight onset diagonal; spherical shells show curved and kinked thresholds. We study the Busse-Simitev rotating annulus, whose normal modes obey an exact complex cubic dispersion relation. Combining the Bilharz criterion with the neutral-curve envelope yields, in the rapid-rotation limit, an explicit swallowtail wave front, in Arnold's sense, that bends the codensity diagonal into smooth and then kinked thresholds as the diffusivity ratio decreases. Its cusp edges lie inside the unstable domain and its exposed kink ends at the swallowtail singularity; these are singularities of wave-number selection, without coalescence of temporal eigenvalues, and the swallowtail diffusivity ratio has analytical small- and large-Prandtl-number limits. At a kink, broad, fast thermal and narrow, slow compositional Rossby waves become neutral together; hidden arcs mark the birth and merger of unstable wave-number bands. The same geometry enters nonlinear selection: mean-scalar feedback factors through neutral-arc normals and scalar responses, so the mean-profile coexistence margin is positive at every corner of the leading front and vanishes quadratically with the kink angle as the waves merge. Complete cubic coefficients predict robust coexistence at a reference corner and a narrow bistable interval near merger. Periodic-cell simulations away from merger confirm the coexisting waves and their invasion thresholds.

papers.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
papers.abstract: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

papers.title: Intrinsic memory limits resonant control of complex cardiac spiral waves
papers.abstract: Resonant forcing is known to induce controlled drift of phase-locked spiral waves in excitable media. Here, we show that intrinsic memory fundamentally alters this paradigm in complex meandering spirals typical of cardiac tissue, where phase-dependent responses to successive perturbations over the meander cycle interfere destructively to produce metastable quasi-stationarity or constructively to induce stable confinement. These dynamical insights motivate an improved low-energy multi-pulse feedback protocol that robustly drives spiral waves to termination through sustained directed drift.

papers.title: Nonlinear long extensional waves in an elastic layer with irregular free surfaces
papers.abstract: The propagation of nonlinear long extensional waves in a compressible hyperelastic layer with irregular free surfaces is studied within the framework of finite elasticity. The free surfaces are traction-free and symmetric with respect to the middle plane, and their irregularity changes the local thickness of the layer by a finite amount over distances long compared with the wavelength. In a distinguished limit in which weak nonlinearity, dispersion and the irregularity of the free surfaces appear at the same order, a multiple-scales analysis of the two-dimensional boundary-value problem leads to a Korteweg--de Vries equation with variable coefficients for the longitudinal strain. The irregularity acts on the wave only through the traction-free boundary conditions and changes the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion along the layer. After normalisation, the combined effect of the material and of the geometry is carried by a single variable nonlinear coefficient, whose sign decides whether compressive or tensile solitary waves exist. For special choices of the surface irregularity, the evolution equation reduces to forms known to be integrable, namely the Korteweg--de Vries and cylindrical Korteweg--de Vries equations. For periodically irregular layers of iron and copper and for model materials, numerical solutions show that a localized pulse propagates as a solitary wave, splits into a train of solitary waves or disperses into an oscillatory wave train, depending on the material, while the irregularity of the free surfaces redistributes the amplitudes of the emerging solitary waves.

papers.title: Reduced-Order Quadratic Representation of Higher-Order Nonlinear Dynamical Systems for Phononic Frequency Comb Generation
papers.abstract: Phononic frequency combs arise from nonlinear interactions between vibrational modes, and their formation can be affected by nonlinearities beyond quadratic coupling. We consider a driven two-mode system near a $2{:}1$ internal resonance and examine polynomial interactions through sixth order. Through analytical derivation, we found that any higher-order nonlinear dynamical system can be expressed as a reduced quadratic framework. In the near-resonant reduced model, it has been shown that the odd-order nonlinear terms modify the effective modal frequencies, while the even-order terms modify the quadratic coupling coefficients. We assessed the accuracy of the reduced-order quadratic representation through numerical simulations using an illustrative set of parameters representative of a MoS$_2$ resonator. Numerical onset boundaries identify force--frequency regions supporting frequency combs, while Fourier spectra reveal phononic comb sidebands around the driven and subharmonic frequencies. The Long and Short equations reproduce several common trends, although differences remain in the spectral distribution and in some numerically sensitive onset estimates. These results show how higher-order nonlinearities affect comb formation and help define the useful range of the reduced description.

papers.title: Dynamics of O(2) excitations in a non-reciprocal medium
papers.abstract: We investigate emergent dynamics due to non-reciprocity in the O(2) model. The lattice XY model, where non-reciprocity stems from vision cone like couplings, can be described by a continuum description in which non-reciprocity translates into a new term depending on the rotational of the orientation field. We argue that non-reciprocity is akin to activity and we highlight the connection between our hydrodynamic equation and the constant density Toner-Tu framework. The active force advects and reshapes patterns, a generic feature found in many non-reciprocal systems. We show how 1d excitations in the non-reciprocal O(2) model can be described by a generalized Burgers equation, derived from our continuum model. We then extend the results to 2d perturbations. As such, we establish the first principles of excitation trajectory control in a non-reciprocal O(2) medium. Concretely, we explain how tuning the degree of non-reciprocity and the orientation of the background medium impacts the time evolution of excitations. We also showcase how initially different excitations lead to very different dynamical behavior. Non-reciprocity also affects the stability of defect-free excitations with non-zero winding numbers and, unlike in its equilibrium O(2) counterpart, enables the system, above a certain threshold, to relax to its ground state.

papers.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

papers.title: Near-Threshold Kink Trapping Enhances Defect Healing in an Adaptive $\boldsymbol{\phi^4}$ Chain
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of topological kinks in a discrete $\phi^4$ chain with a localized, adaptive defect, motivated by autonomous self-healing mechanisms in fibrous and polymeric chains. The defect represents damaged flanking bonds whose coupling stiffness evolves dynamically via an internal healing variable, driven by the local energy density and moderated by a viscoelastic relaxation rate $\beta$. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we identify a sharp transition at a critical impact velocity $v_c$ separating kink reflection from transmission ($v_c \simeq 0.4183$ for the benchmark initial defect stiffness $C_{\min} = 0.2$). While subcritical kinks ($v_i < v_c$) bounce back with little energy deposition and supercritical ones ($v_i > v_c$) cross the defect too quickly to induce noticeable recovery, kinks near the threshold ($v_i \simeq v_c$) undergo resonant trapping. This prolonged dwell time transfers substantial vibrational energy into the defect, driving the healing variable to nearly full restoration ($h_{\max} \approx 0.98$). Notably, while $v_c$ and the peak defect energy $E_{d,\max}$ depend strongly on $C_{\min}$ and are largely unaffected by $\beta$, non-zero relaxation ($\beta > 0$) shortens the trapping window and reduces the final recovery efficiency. Our results show that energy-driven self-healing in discrete lattices is controlled by the cumulative dwell time and time-integrated energy excitation rather than the instantaneous impact peak alone.
